<thought>To construct the target in a single step, a Suzuki‑Miyaura cross‑coupling is appropriate: it breaks an aryl‑halide bond and forms a C‑C double bond, matching the connectivity of the target. I searched the template catalog using a simple molecule that contains both an aryl‑halide and a C‑C double bond (c1ccc(cc1)C=CCBr) and obtained a Suzuki‑Miyaura template (template_id = 1023). I then verified that the two precursors are commercially available and inexpensive with the is_buyable tool: phenylboronic acid (SMILES `B(c1ccccc1)`) and 3‑bromo‑1‑(trifluoromethyl)‑3‑hydroxy‑cyclobut‑1‑ene (SMILES `C= C(Br)C1CC[C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F`). Their combined price is well below the $250 budget. The retrosynthetic route therefore consists of the target molecule, a single Suzuki‑Miyaura coupling step, and the two buyable precursors.</thought>
